onboarding.consentIntro: Here’s how we handle your health information.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.body: Health Journal organizes your records and gives health information. It isn't a doctor, pharmacist or emergency service.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.body: Your data is private to your account, encrypted in transit and at rest, and stored by Supabase in Frankfurt, Germany. Export or delete it anytime.

health_data_processing.title: Storing your health info
health_data_processing.body: We store the records, documents and medications you add so you can follow them over time.

ai_processing.title: AI reading
ai_processing.body: Lets the app send your documents and related records to a secure AI model to read reports and answer your questions. Your data never trains AI models. Without it, you can still type results in yourself.

review.title: Check your results
review.subtitle: Results we read clearly are at the bottom. Only the ones below need a check.
review.duplicate: A confirmed report from the same date has nearly identical results. If it’s the same report, discard this copy.
review.dateFallback: Only a report date was found, so we used it as the collection date. I've checked it.
review.dateUncertain: Day and month may be swapped on this report. I've checked the date.
review.unitNotComparable: This unit can't convert to {{unit}}, so it won't be compared with your other results for this test.
review.unmatchedHint: Not in our list yet. We'll still track it by its printed name and unit. Pick the test if you know it and we'll remember next time.
review.checkedAgainstDoc: I've checked the highlighted fields against the document

problems.name: Every result needs a test name.
problems.unchecked: Check the highlighted fields and tick the box under each.

review.saveError: Couldn't save. Nothing changed; try again.
review.discardConfirm: Discard this report? Its draft results won't be saved.
review.notFound: This report isn't available to review.

matchSource.shared: known name, confirmed by other users

review.aiMatchUnit: Looks like {{test}}, but the unit doesn't fit. Pick the test if you're sure.

report.sourceNote: Values come from your confirmed report. Labels compare each value with the lab’s printed range. They aren’t a diagnosis.
report.notComparable: Not compared: the unit or date doesn't match your other results.
report.byNameOnly: Compared by printed name and unit only, since this test isn't in our list yet.
report.unrecognized: Not in our list yet. Future results with the same name and unit will be compared to this one.
report.removeConfirm: Remove this result? The original stays in the change log.
report.correctionNote: The original value stays in the change log. All comparisons will use the corrected one.

liver.borderline: Borderline ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). On its own, this doesn't mean liver damage. Worth bringing up at your next visit.
liver.mild: Mild elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). Talk to your doctor, who may suggest a repeat test.
liver.moderate: Moderate elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). Contact your doctor soon to go over it.
liver.severe: Marked elevation ({{fold}}× the lab's upper limit). Contact your doctor today.
liver.massive: Very high result. Seek medical care today.

history.notFound: No results found for this test.
history.noNumeric: No numeric results to chart for this test.
history.notCompared: Not included (a different unit we can't convert)

level.urgent: Urgent medical attention may be needed

critical_value.title: {{test}} needs prompt medical attention
critical_value.body: Your {{test}} of {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} is past a limit labs treat as critical.
critical_value.action: Call your doctor today. If you feel unwell, call {{emergency}} or go to the nearest ER.

outside_range_high.title: {{test}} is above the lab's range
outside_range_high.body: {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} (lab range {{range}}). One result outside the range is common and isn't a diagnosis on its own.
outside_range_high.action: Bring it up at your next visit.

outside_range_low.title: {{test}} is below the lab's range
outside_range_low.body: {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} (lab range {{range}}). One result outside the range is common and isn't a diagnosis on its own.
outside_range_low.action: Bring it up at your next visit.

ldl_severe_190.title: LDL cholesterol is 190 mg/dL or higher
ldl_severe_190.body: Your LDL of {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} is in the range that cholesterol guidelines treat as severely high.

hba1c_diabetes_range.title: HbA1c is in the diabetes range
hba1c_diabetes_range.body: {{value}}{{unit}} on {{date}} is 6.5% or higher, the range used to diagnose diabetes. One result isn't a diagnosis; guidelines call for a confirming test.

hba1c_prediabetes_range.title: HbA1c is in the prediabetes range
hba1c_prediabetes_range.body: {{value}}{{unit}} on {{date}} is between 5.7% and 6.4%, the range guidelines call prediabetes.
hba1c_prediabetes_range.action: Worth bringing up at your next visit.

egfr_category.title: Kidney filtration (eGFR) is in category {{category}}
egfr_category.body: {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}}. Category {{category}} means kidney filtration is lower than normal.
egfr_category.action: Discuss it with your doctor, who may repeat the test.

trend_improving.title: {{test}} has improved
trend_improving.body: From {{previousValue}} on {{previousDate}} to {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} ({{percent}}). That's more than normal day-to-day variation.

trend_worsening.title: {{test}} moved further outside the lab's range
trend_worsening.body: From {{previousValue}} on {{previousDate}} to {{value}} {{unit}} on {{date}} ({{percent}}). That's more than normal day-to-day variation.
trend_worsening.action: Worth bringing up at your next visit.

vitals.title: Readings
vitals.subtitle: What you check at home: blood pressure, blood sugar, weight, heart rate, oxygen and temperature.
vitals.notePlaceholder: e.g., after a walk, felt dizzy

invalid.blood_pressure: Enter both numbers. The top one should be higher.
invalid.heart_rate: Enter a heart rate between 20 and 250.
invalid.oxygen: Enter an oxygen level between 50 and 100%.

vitals.oneReading: One reading doesn't diagnose anything. Doctors look at averages over several days.
vitals.childNote: These blood pressure categories are for adults. Kids' ranges depend on age and height, so ask their doctor.
vitals.addHeight: Add your height in your profile to see BMI.

band.blood_pressure: Shaded: normal to elevated top number (90–129).
band.glucose: Shaded: usual pre-meal target for people with diabetes.
band.heart_rate: Shaded: normal resting range for adults (60–100).

empty.blood_pressure: No blood pressure readings yet. Checking at the same time each morning gives the most useful average.
empty.weight: No weigh-ins yet. Once a week is plenty.
empty.heart_rate: No heart rate readings yet. Check at rest, at the same time each day.

meaning.bp_normal: This reading is in the normal range for adults.
meaning.bp_elevated: Slightly above normal. Healthy habits help keep it from climbing. Mention it at your next checkup if your average stays here.
meaning.bp_stage1: In the range doctors call stage 1 high blood pressure. Don't judge by one reading: if your average stays here, discuss it with your doctor.
meaning.bp_stage2: In the range doctors call stage 2 high blood pressure. If your average stays here, contact your doctor soon.
meaning.bp_severe: Very high. Wait 5 minutes and measure again. If it's still this high, contact your doctor right away. If you also have chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness or weakness, vision changes or trouble speaking, call emergency services now.
meaning.bp_low: Lower than usual. If you feel dizzy, faint or unwell, contact your doctor.
meaning.glucose_very_low: Very low blood sugar. Treat it now as your care team taught you, for example 15 g of fast-acting sugar (like half a cup of juice), then check again in 15 minutes. If you feel confused, can't eat or drink, or don't improve, get emergency help.
meaning.glucose_low: Low blood sugar. Have some fast-acting sugar and check again in 15 minutes. If this happens often, tell your doctor.
meaning.glucose_very_high: Very high. Contact your doctor today. If you're vomiting, very thirsty, drowsy or confused, get urgent care.
meaning.glucose_in_target: Within the usual target for people with diabetes at this time of day.
meaning.glucose_above_target: Above the usual target for this time. If many readings are like this, discuss it with your doctor.
meaning.glucose_fasting_raised: A fasting level of 100–125 mg/dL can be a sign of prediabetes. One home reading doesn't diagnose it; ask your doctor about a lab test.
meaning.glucose_fasting_high: A fasting level of 126 mg/dL or more is in the diabetes range. One home reading doesn't diagnose it; contact your doctor for a lab test.
meaning.glucose_high_random: 200 mg/dL or more at any time is high. Contact your doctor, especially if you're very thirsty or passing urine often.
meaning.bmi_under: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the underweight range.
meaning.bmi_healthy: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the healthy range.
meaning.bmi_over: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the overweight range. BMI doesn't account for muscle; your doctor can tell you what it means for you.
meaning.bmi_obesity: Your BMI (from your height and weight) is in the obesity range. BMI doesn't account for muscle; your doctor can tell you what it means for you.
meaning.hr_normal: A normal resting heart rate for adults.
meaning.hr_low: Below 60 at rest. This can be normal for fit people or with some medications. If you feel dizzy, faint or short of breath, contact your doctor.
meaning.hr_high: Above 100 at rest. Rest for a few minutes and measure again. If it stays high or you feel chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath, contact your doctor; with chest pain or fainting, call emergency services.
meaning.spo2_normal: In the usual range. If your doctor gave you a different target, follow theirs.
meaning.spo2_borderline: 93–94% is a little lower than usual. Warm your hands, sit still and measure again. If it stays here or you feel unwell, contact your doctor. If your doctor gave you a different target, follow theirs.
meaning.spo2_low: 92% or lower: contact your doctor today. Measure again with warm hands first. Readings can be less accurate on darker skin, cold fingers or with nail polish. If your doctor gave you a different target (e.g. for COPD), follow theirs.
meaning.temp_fever: 38°C (100.4°F) or above is a fever. Rest and drink fluids. Contact your doctor if it lasts more than 3 days, or if you feel very unwell.
meaning.temp_very_high: 40°C (104°F) or above is a high fever. Contact your doctor today. Get urgent help if there's confusion, a stiff neck, a rash that doesn't fade under a glass, or trouble breathing.
meaning.temp_fever_baby: A baby under 3 months with 38°C (100.4°F) or above needs urgent medical advice now. For older babies, contact their doctor.
meaning.temp_low: Below 35°C (95°F) can be dangerous (hypothermia). Measure again; if it's still this low, get urgent medical help, especially for older people and babies.
meaning.spo2_very_low: 88% or lower: get immediate medical attention, especially if you're short of breath, confused, or your lips look bluish.

vitals.restingHint: Measure after sitting quietly for 5 minutes.

voice.title: Say it
